Updates `mermaid` from 11.17.2 to 12.0.0
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]">mermaid's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>mermaid@12.0.0</h2>
<p><strong>Mermaid 12.0.0</strong> ships ELK as the bundled default layout engine, a new <code>redux-color</code> / <code>neo</code> default appearance, and two new diagram types: <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: mermaid.ai]">UML use case diagrams</a>.</p>
<p>This is a breaking release (ES2024, Safari 17.4+, Node 22.12+). Existing flowcharts, state and class diagrams will re-lay out and recolour; add <code>layout: dagre</code>, <code>theme: default</code> and <code>look: classic</code> to your config to keep the old look. Full changelog below.</p>
<h3>Major Changes</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p><a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: redirect.github.com]">#8213</a> <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>33442fd</code></a> Thanks <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>@​aloisklink</code></a>! - chore!: require ES2024, Safari 17.4+, Node.JS v22.12+</p>
<p>Mermaid is now built to target Safari 17.4+ and ES2024. If you need to support
older browsers, you may need to polyfill or transpile mermaid.</p>
<p>Safari 17.4+ has been chosen as the floor, as unlike Firefox/Chrome,
older iOS devices don't get major Safari updates.</p>
<p>Node.JS v22.12+ is also declared as requirement in our <code>package.json</code> files,
but as mermaid requires a browser, this is mainly so we can use dependencies that
also declare a Node.JS v22.12+ requirement, without causing issues for users when
running <code>npm install</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: redirect.github.com]">#8155</a> <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>810893c</code></a> Thanks <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>@​ashishjain0512</code></a>! - feat!: <strong>ELK is now bundled with mermaid and is the default layout algorithm.</strong></p>
<p>ELK previously shipped as a separate <code>@mermaid-js/layout-elk</code> package that sites had to install and register. It is now part of mermaid itself and registered automatically, so <code>layout: elk</code> — and the <code>elk.stress</code>, <code>elk.force</code>, <code>elk.mrtree</code>, <code>elk.sporeOverlap</code>, <code>elk.box</code> and <code>elk.rectpacking</code> variants — work with no setup.</p>
<p><strong>This changes how existing diagrams look.</strong> Flowchart, state, class, entity-relationship, requirement, use-case diagrams that do not specify a <code>layout</code> are now laid out by ELK instead of dagre. To keep the previous layout, set dagre explicitly:</p>
<pre lang="yaml"><code>---
config:
  layout: dagre
---
</code></pre>
<p>or globally, <code>mermaid.initialize({ layout: 'dagre' })</code>.</p>
<p>Mindmap is unchanged: it keeps laying out with cose-bilkent unless a layout is explicitly requested (in the tiny build, which ships neither ELK nor cose-bilkent, it falls back to dagre).</p>
<p>Other notes:</p>
<ul>
<li>ELK is loaded as a separate chunk in the ESM builds, so it is only fetched when a diagram actually uses it. The single-file IIFE build (<code>mermaid.min.js</code>) inlines it and grows by roughly 500 kB gzipped.</li>
<li>The <strong>tiny</strong> build deliberately omits ELK to stay small, and falls back to dagre for diagrams that ask for an ELK layout. Its size is unchanged.</li>
<li><code>@mermaid-js/layout-elk</code> is no longer needed on normal builds — existing <code>mermaid.registerLayoutLoaders(elkLayouts)</code> calls keep working and can be removed. It is still published, and remains the way to add ELK to the tiny build.</li>
<li><code>dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs</code> now contains syntax that <code>es-module-lexer</code> (used by Vite) rejects with <code>content contains invalid JS syntax</code>. Bundler users are unaffected as long as they import the <code>mermaid</code> package specifier, which resolves to the core build; only builds that point Vite directly at that dist file need to switch to the package specifier or the core build.</li>
<li>State diagrams now resolve their layout through the same registration check as every other diagram, so an unavailable layout falls back instead of failing to render.</li>
</ul>
<p>An unrecognised <code>theme</code> name now resolves to the default theme in name as well as in variables; previously the invalid name stayed in place while the default's variables were loaded, and every palette-aware stylesheet gates on the name. <code>theme: 'null'</code>, the documented way to disable the pre-defined themes, is unaffected. Note that <code>neo</code> paints node strokes with a gradient when the theme sets <code>useGradient</code>, which <code>base</code> does; setting a custom <code>nodeBorder</code> on <code>base</code> turns the gradient off.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: redirect.github.com]">#8211</a> <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>a19bd08</code></a> Thanks <a href="[QUARANTINED_URL: github.com]"><code>@​ashishjain0512</code></a>! - <strong>Removed: the <code>defaultRenderer</code> option of the <code>flowchart</code>, <code>class</code> and <code>state</code> config sections.</strong></p>
<p>Use the top-level <code>layout</code> option instead:</p>
</li>
</ul>

## Comments

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-09-14T17:55:53Z

## The e2e red was a flake, and it was not mermaid — but the mermaid bump is worth one decision

`gh pr checks` now exits 0 on `f008d2cdb3`: **all checks green, MERGEABLE/CLEAN.**

### The failure

`e2e/grid/ThumbDragPause.spec.mjs:49` — `expect(blankFrames.length).toBe(0)`, received 10, `rowCount→frames {"42":10}` spanning 142ms. A frame-sampling assertion over a paused thumb drag on `/examples/grid/bigData/index.html`. **No mermaid on that path** — not in the spec, not in the example.

### Why it is a flake and not this PR

`dev` itself went red in the same tier ~10 hours later, at `019286b770`, on a **different** spec — `e2e/grid/HeaderCellRectSync.spec.mjs:99`, `no cell under header "Private %"` mid-drag. That head's only new commit is a test-only change to two `neuralLink` specs that CI deselects, so it cannot have caused it either.

Both jobs re-run at their **unchanged heads**:

| head | first run | re-run |
|---|---|---|
| `f008d2cdb3` (this PR) | `ThumbDragPause` ✘ | ✅ |
| `019286b770` (dev) | `HeaderCellRectSync` ✘ | ✅ |

Two different drag-timing specs, two heads, neither diff able to explain its own failure, both green on re-run. That is environment, not code.

### The mermaid bump, tested rather than assumed

`11.17.2 → 12.0.0` is a major, and the instinct to suspect it is right in general — **but nothing in CI would have caught a v12 break.** `e2e/portal/LearnMermaidRender.spec.mjs` is outside `RUN_PATHS` (its precondition — a visible Monaco editor in a live preview — does not hold on a hosted runner), and `unit/component/MermaidTheme.spec.mjs` tests theme *resolution* as a pure function and never loads the library. So the green above says nothing about mermaid either way.

Ran the A/B by hand — a worktree at this PR's head with `npm ci`, the browser bundles built, against the same specs on `dev`'s v11:

| | mermaid | `LearnMermaidRender` |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` checkout | 11.17.2 | 2 passed, 1 failed |
| worktree @ `f008d2cdb3` | 12.0.0 | 2 passed, 1 failed — **same arm, byte-identical error** |

The shared failure is `Expected: 2 / Received: 4` — "every mermaid fence in `DockLayouts.md` must reach the reader as an SVG". That is **#18675** (the guide renders its whole body twice), open and unowned, and present on both versions. `MermaidTheme` 13/13 on v12.

`buildScripts/build/mermaid.mjs` bundles v12 cleanly: `0 UMD registrations`, so the Monaco-AMD collision the bundler exists to prevent does not return.

### The one thing that actually changes

**`dist/mermaid.mjs` grows 3,452,330 → 5,343,805 bytes (+55%).** That file ships — the build script's own note records that `.npmignore` forces a single bundled file because mermaid and esbuild are both devDependencies, so every consumer takes it. A decision, not a defect: it is the price of v12, and it is worth being deliberate about rather than discovering downstream.

Evidence: L3 (mounted e2e, both dependency sets, plus CI re-runs at unchanged heads) → L3 required. Residual: none for the flake; the bundle-size question is a judgement, not a measurement gap.
